title: the question tool's both-ends probe reads the artifact trail, not the index
intention: both_ends_agree reads every question and answer event from artifact.read_trail, so an open and its answer on one question file are both seen. The trail is per box and keeps 30 days; this reader sees only that, and says so.
traces_to: Law 3: a probe that sees one event per question file cannot measure whether both ends agreed.
how: Swap the probe's journal read for door.read_trail(root). The docstring and the finding name the 30-day, per-box horizon. It builds after b15da5656579 lands, which adds read_trail and the index.

clauses.claim: one question opened and answered through a scratch world's door gives the probe both events
the probe's finding names the 30-day horizon

why: Split from b15da5656579 under RULE 1. Akien, 16:47 UTC 2026-11-16, relayed verbatim by the orchestrator: "then how about this... the latest entry remains in cairn commons, and everything else broken into... per day? per week? inside of our .cairn/logs folder". After b15d the journal holds only the newest entry per path and every entry is in a day trail on this box for 30 days.

decisions.text: D1: the reader reads as the intention says.
D2: the red-first proof, one tooth per clause.

out: every other component; cairn/tools/artifact is b15da5656579's

measured.saw: cairn/tools/question/probes/both_ends_agree.py read the journal in the way b15da5656579 changes
measured.how: git grep for read_journal and .artifact-journal over the cairn tree, each hit read (b15da5656579's census)
